steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The Solar System consists of the Sun and everything gravitationally bound to it

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Eight planets orbit the Sun: four terrestrial (Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars) and four gas/ice giants (Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune)

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Dwarf planets include Pluto, Ceres, Eris, Haumea and Makemake

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The asteroid belt lies between Mars and Jupiter

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Q: Name the four terrestrial planets in order from the Sun. | Q: What is the asteroid belt and where is it located? | Q: Explain why Pluto is classified as a dwarf planet rather than a planet.

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars | A region between Mars and Jupiter containing many rocky bodies; it separates the inner and outer planets. | Pluto has not cleared its orbital neighbourhood of other debris, which is one of the three IAU criteria for full planet status. It orbits the Sun and is spherical, but fails the clearing criterion.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Remember the order of planets using mnemonics (e.g. My Very Easy Method Just Speeds Up Naming) Dwarf planets fail the 'clearing orbit' criterion — this is the key distinction The Oort cloud is theoretical — we infer its existence from long-period comets Both AQA and Edexcel expect you to know the difference between terrestrial and gas/ice giants
